alignments.note: Inferential particle rendered by the single connective *Therefore*.

Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32); the ASV writes two words, *he* and *that*, so the ordinary split applies and rule 90's single-word case does not arise.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer *that* is a rule 7 helper on the participle, headed on the lexical verb *rejecteth* (t004, the first of the two).
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*; no second negative word stands, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise.
Anarthrous accusative object rendered by the bare noun *man*.
Finite verb takes the second *rejecteth* (t005); the first belongs to the participle s003.
Article governing θεόν has no English realization: the ASV writes a bare *God* with no determiner, so rule 23 applies and rule 21 forbids leaving a bare case word on it.

Second attributive article following the expressed head noun θεόν. Rule 31's test: the article governs an expressed head noun, exactly as τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created*, so the article realizes nothing and the relativizer *who* is the participle's helper. Rule 90 is not in point, blessing no unit in which a head noun is expressed.
Intensifying καί; the ASV writes no *also* or *even* for it, so rule 65's English-side test leaves it empty.
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *who* is a rule 7 helper on it under rule 31, headed on the lexical verb *giveth*.

Article displaced by the possessive *his*, which the genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ licenses (rule 20); that pronoun is free and carries nothing else, so it is rule 20 proper rather than rule 76's availability arm.
Genitive pronoun carries the English possessive *his*.
Second attributive article in τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον has no English realization (rule 23).

review_notes: Both variant units leave the projection carrying material the ASV translates, so rule 97 is not in play: v005 (καί, underdetermined to r00-base) and v006 (διδόντα, selected r00-base) are aligned or emptied on ordinary grounds.
The two occurrences of *rejecteth* are kept apart: t004 with the participle s003 and t005 with the finite s006, following the English order.

s010 is left unrepresented under rule 31 because θεόν is an expressed head noun standing in front of the article; reading it under rule 90 as taking *who* would be the competing analysis, and rule 90 excludes itself where a head noun is expressed.
